description:
Team: BEYOND THE UNIVERSE
 I am Ruchika, an independent researcher from Punjab, India. My project explores what lies beyond the observable universe through the lens of Vacuum-Energy. This research proposes Vacuum-Energy as a driving force for expansion beyond the observable limit and presents a theoretical framework linking quantum vacuum with cosmic expansion. This is a solo research submission. My paper is published with DOI on Zenodo.
summary:
The Silence Between Worlds explores what lies beyond the observable universe through the lens of vacuum and time.
Our universe is expanding, and distant galaxies are moving away faster than light can travel. This means there are regions we will never see, not because they do not exist, but because their light will never reach us. We call this the cosmic silence. 
Our project explains this idea using NASA data on cosmic expansion, exoplanets, and the observable universe. We show how two worlds can exist in the same universe, yet their time never matches. One world moves forward, while the other remains frozen in silence.
details:
Our project, The Silence Between Worlds, explains the concept of the observable universe and cosmic silence through a simple visual story.
The universe is expanding, and light from distant galaxies takes time to reach us. Because of this expansion, some parts of the universe are moving away faster than light, so we will never see them. This is the silence we explore.
We used NASA data on cosmic expansion, the observable universe, and exoplanets to build our idea. Our project shows two worlds in the same universe, where one moves forward in time and the other remains frozen in silence.
We created a 30-second video and visuals using Canva and video editing tools to make this difficult concept easy for students and the public to understand. Our goal is to inspire curiosity about what lies beyond what we can see, and to show that space is not only what we observe, but also what we will never hear.
